paragraphs: Multi-objective reinforcement learning studies agents that must pursue several goals, potentially with competing demands. Each goal has its own reward function, so evaluating an algorithm involves more than optimizing a single reward. This paper introduces a coordinated software toolkit to make research and comparisons in this setting easier to carry out.

The first component, MO-Gymnasium, provides a common interface for building environments and includes more than 20 environments. The second, MORL-Baselines, supplies implementations of established multi-objective learning algorithms. These implementations are compatible with MO-Gymnasium, connecting the environments and algorithms through a shared foundation rather than requiring separate integration for each comparison.

The third component is a collection of benchmark results across challenging environments. These comparisons are intended to clarify the properties, strengths, and limitations of the included methods. Together, the libraries and benchmarks provide both reusable experimental infrastructure and reference results. The contribution is a practical foundation for studying how different algorithms handle multiple objectives and for evaluating new approaches within the same framework.
neurips-2023-a-toolkit-for-reliable-benc.tldr: A coordinated toolkit combines multi-objective reinforcement learning environments, compatible algorithm implementations, and benchmark comparisons.

paragraphs: Predictive models can fail when relationships between class labels and nuisance factors change after training. This paper considers settings with additional metadata labels that describe those factors. Its central assumption is that the joint frequencies of classes and metadata may change across domains, while the distribution of features conditional on both remains fixed.

The proposed Test-Time Label-Shift Adaptation method treats each class and metadata combination as part of an expanded label space. It uses expectation maximization on unlabeled target-domain examples to adapt to changes in the joint label distribution. This covers changes in class frequencies, nuisance-factor frequencies, or the association between them.

The procedure only needs to reweight the outputs of a discriminative model trained to predict classes and metadata jointly. It avoids directly fitting a model that generates features from those labels. Experiments on image, text, and CheXpert chest X-ray datasets report improvements over methods targeting invariance and over empirical risk minimization baselines. The results support adaptation under the stated shift model, where changing label relationships can be estimated from target data.
neurips-2023-beyond-invariance-test-time.tldr: TTLSA adapts predictions to changing class–metadata frequencies using unlabeled target data under an expanded label-shift assumption.

paragraphs: Prior theory suggests that very deep networks with L2 regularization favor low-dimensional internal representations. This tendency can be described through a function-level rank quantity, whose identification with Bottleneck rank was conjectured. The paper examines how finite depth changes this picture, revealing a tradeoff between reducing dimension and keeping feature maps regular.

The authors derive a correction term measuring regularity. It bounds a quantity built from the Jacobian's nonzero singular values and is subadditive under both addition and composition. These properties formalize why representation dimension alone does not capture the full preference induced by regularization: the complexity of the maps producing those representations also matters.

The paper also proves a bottleneck structure in the infinite-depth limit. At large depths, almost all hidden representations are approximately as dimensional as the rank quantity. Almost all weight matrices have that many singular values near one, with the others shrinking at order L to the minus one-half. Within the analysis, large learning rates are required for a neural tangent kernel scaling that guarantees convergence of almost all layers' representations.
neurips-2023-bottleneck-structure-in-lea.tldr: The analysis shows how depth and L2 regularization balance low-dimensional features against regularity and produce an asymptotic bottleneck structure.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a bandit model that brings together cascading bandits and assortment bandits. The combined model, called cascading contextual assortment bandits, broadens the decision settings these existing formulations can represent. The authors develop two algorithms and analyze regret, which measures the accumulated cost of learning rather than making the best decisions throughout.

The first algorithm, UCB-CCA, has a regret upper bound scaling as d times the square root of T, divided by a problem-dependent constant kappa, up to logarithmic factors. Its improvement over existing cascading contextual bandit bounds is the removal of dependence on cascade length K. Thus, cascade length no longer appears as a factor in this guarantee.

The second algorithm, UCB-CCA+, uses a new Bernstein-type concentration result to sharpen the treatment of uncertainty. Its leading regret term scales as d times the square root of T without dependence on kappa, again up to logarithmic factors. This is specifically a leading-term improvement. Numerical experiments support the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed methods.
neurips-2023-cascading-contextual-assort.tldr: Two algorithms for a unified cascading assortment bandit model improve regret bounds by removing cascade-length and leading-term kappa dependence.

paragraphs: Complex-valued neural networks have shown empirical promise, but their theoretical advantages over real-valued networks are less clear. This paper studies a focused version of that comparison: which single-neuron functions gradient descent can learn, and how quickly it learns them. The results distinguish expressive capability from optimization speed.

The authors show that a complex-valued neuron can learn a function represented by any single real-valued neuron or any single complex-valued neuron. The respective convergence upper bounds are O(t^-3) and O(t^-1), where t counts gradient descent iterations. They also establish that a finite-width, two-layer real-valued network cannot learn a single non-degenerate complex-valued neuron in the studied setting.

That greater capability comes with a speed tradeoff. For a real-valued teacher neuron, the complex-valued learner has an Omega(t^-3) lower bound, whereas a real-valued learner achieves an exponentially decreasing rate, O(exp(-ct)). Thus, the more expressive learner can be substantially slower on a target the simpler learner already represents. Simulations verify the theoretical findings and extend the investigation to more general settings.
neurips-2023-complex-valued-neurons-can-.tldr: Complex-valued neurons can learn a broader class of single-neuron targets, but learning real-valued targets can be much slower.

paragraphs: Optical flow usually describes how pixels move between consecutive video frames. This paper develops a representation of dense motion that varies continuously over time. The aim is to turn separate frame-to-frame correspondences into trajectories that describe motion across an arbitrary time interval, making continuity part of the representation itself.

The method fits point trajectories with B-splines using a limited number of frames. These provide an explicit temporal model of motion. An additional encoder based on a neural ordinary differential equation represents features associated with particular times. Combining the trajectory model with learned time-dependent features is intended to improve the stability and robustness of the resulting paths.

The authors also contribute a synthetic dataset and two evaluation perspectives for assessing continuous-flow accuracy and robustness. Their model outperforms the evaluated flow-based and point-tracking approaches when fitting long-term and variable sequences. The stated findings support combining explicit motion curves with implicit feature optimization: the curves organize motion over time, while the feature model helps refine the trajectories.
neurips-2023-continuous-parametric-optic.tldr: Continuous parametric optical flow combines B-spline trajectories with neural differential-equation features to estimate continuous motion from video frames.

paragraphs: Systematic literature reviews depend on identifying relevant studies from a larger body of publications. Machine learning can help automate this screening, but evaluating competing systems requires suitable shared datasets. The paper examines existing evaluation resources and finds problems with small size, data leakage, and applicability across different ways of formulating the screening task.

To improve that foundation, the authors introduce CSMED, a meta-dataset combining nine publicly released collections. It provides unified access to 325 systematic reviews in medicine and computer science. Consolidating these resources creates a common basis for training and evaluating citation-screening models, addressing fragmentation in the available evidence for comparing systems.

The paper also introduces CSMED-FT, a new dataset specifically for evaluating screening based on full publication text. This adds an evaluation resource for a distinct part of the review workflow. Experiments establish baselines on the new datasets and demonstrate their use. The main contribution is therefore evaluation infrastructure: organized data and reference results that support more consistent investigation of automated literature screening.
neurips-2023-csmed-bridging-the-dataset-.tldr: CSMED unifies citation-screening data from 325 systematic reviews and adds a dedicated dataset for full-text screening.

paragraphs: Tensor decomposition analyzes data organized along several dimensions, but sparse observations can still contain valuable timing and relationship information. The paper proposes DEMOTE to use both sources of structure. Instead of assigning each entity an unchanging representation, it learns embedding trajectories that evolve over time.

DEMOTE builds a multipartite graph from observed tensor entries to encode correlations between entities. A graph diffusion process couples the trajectories of related entities, while a neural reaction process models each entity's individual evolution. This division lets the model represent shared patterns and entity-specific behavior together. Another neural network predicts tensor-entry values as nonlinear functions of those evolving representations.

For learning, the authors combine ordinary differential equation solvers with stochastic minibatch optimization. They also introduce stratified sampling to balance the processing cost of minibatches and improve overall efficiency. Simulation studies and real-world applications show advantages for the approach. The contribution connects temporal modeling with the structure already present in sparse observations, rather than treating those two sources of information separately.
neurips-2023-dynamic-tensor-decompositio.tldr: DEMOTE models time-varying tensor data with coupled graph diffusion and entity-specific neural reactions.

paragraphs: Evaluating a final math answer alone can hide where a language model's reasoning or tool use went wrong. This paper introduces CARP, a Chinese dataset containing 4,886 computation-intensive algebra problems with annotations for intermediate steps. These annotations make it possible to examine the solution process as well as its outcome.

Tests of four language models using chain-of-thought prompting reveal a tendency to make errors early in solutions, leading to incorrect answers. The authors respond with DELI, an approach that revisits intermediate reasoning. It first generates a step-by-step solution using retrieved examples, then repeatedly checks and refines that solution.

DELI alternates two deliberation procedures, one addressing tool manipulation and the other natural-language reasoning. Iteration stops when solutions converge or a maximum iteration count is reached. Across CARP and six other datasets, DELI mostly outperforms competitive baselines and can improve existing chain-of-thought methods. The findings support evaluating and revising the intermediate process, especially when successful reasoning requires coordinating calculations with tool interfaces.
neurips-2023-evaluating-and-improving-to.tldr: CARP evaluates intermediate mathematical reasoning, while DELI improves solutions by repeatedly checking tool use and reasoning steps.

paragraphs: This paper strengthens theoretical guarantees for Thompson Sampling in reinforcement learning. Its focus is Bayesian regret, a measure of the accumulated performance cost of learning under uncertainty about the environment. The contribution is a refined analysis that yields improved bounds across several kinds of environment models.

The central result concerns time-inhomogeneous reinforcement learning, where dynamics can depend on the position within an episode. The regret upper bound has order H times the square root of d_l1 T, up to logarithmic factors. Here H is episode length, and d_l1 is the Kolmogorov l1-dimension of the environment space. This dimension provides the complexity quantity through which the bound reflects the set of possible environments.

The proof uses a sharper analysis of the information ratio. The authors then bound the environment dimension for tabular models, linear models, and finite mixtures, turning the general result into concrete guarantees. These applications show how one analysis can cover different forms of structure and improve existing Bayesian regret results in the settings studied.
neurips-2023-improved-bayesian-regret-bo.tldr: A refined information-ratio analysis improves Thompson Sampling's Bayesian regret guarantees across several reinforcement learning settings.

paragraphs: A dynamic network can be recorded as interactions between pairs of entities, each with a timestamp. Intensity Profile Projection turns these events into a continuous trajectory for every node. The trajectory represents how that node's behavior changes over time, providing an evolving representation directly from timestamped interactions.

The framework has three stages. It first estimates how pairwise interaction intensities vary over time, for example through kernel smoothing. It then learns a projection that minimizes an intensity reconstruction error. Finally, it applies that projection to construct the node trajectories. The resulting representations satisfy the structural and temporal coherence properties that the authors identify as important for reliable inference.

The paper also develops estimation theory that tightly controls trajectory error. This suggests the representations could support downstream analyses sensitive to noise. The theory explains smoothing as a balance between bias and variance, and shows that less smoothing is possible as the signal-to-noise ratio increases. Sharing information across the network helps the method estimate individual trajectories more effectively.
neurips-2023-intensity-profile-projectio.tldr: Intensity Profile Projection converts timestamped network interactions into coherent continuous node trajectories with theoretical error control.

paragraphs: Conditional independence testing asks whether two variables remain related after accounting for other variables. It becomes difficult when the conditioning information has many dimensions or the dataset is small. This paper proposes a test combining a classifier-based estimate of conditional mutual information with local sampling based on nearest neighbors.

The classifier estimates potentially complex dependence, while nearest-neighbor sampling approximates a distribution representing the independence hypothesis. The method does not require specified distributional forms or assumptions about feature dependencies. It also avoids splitting the dataset and deriving an asymptotic null distribution for the information estimate, features that make it particularly relevant when samples are scarce.

The authors establish asymptotic control of false positives and consistency against all alternative hypotheses. These are large-sample guarantees rather than an assertion of exact finite-sample error control. Synthetic and real-data evaluations show computational efficiency and lower type I and type II errors than the compared state-of-the-art methods, including with high-dimensional conditioning variables. The reported experiments also show robustness with heavy-tailed data.
neurips-2023-k-nearest-neighbor-local-sa.tldr: A classifier-based conditional independence test uses nearest-neighbor sampling to support efficient testing with high-dimensional conditioning variables.

paragraphs: A network may fit its training data perfectly in many different ways, making the solution favored by training an important question. This paper studies that question for learning a single teacher neuron with a one-hidden-layer ReLU network. It considers gradient flow from a small initialization and assumes that training points are correlated with the teacher neuron.

Under the studied conditions, the authors prove convergence to zero loss for networks of any width. They also show an implicit preference for minimizing the rank of the network parameters. The argument tracks the dynamics of each hidden neuron through a detailed non-asymptotic analysis, extending understanding beyond earlier work on orthogonal datasets.

The paper further distinguishes minimum-rank interpolating networks from those with minimum Euclidean norm. Although both describe simple solutions in different senses, they need not coincide in this setting. Characterizing that difference clarifies what kind of simplicity the training dynamics favor. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical findings about convergence, parameter rank, and the distinction between these solution criteria.
neurips-2023-learning-a-neuron-by-a-shal.tldr: For the studied correlated-input setting, gradient flow learns a single neuron with a shallow ReLU network while favoring low-rank parameters.

paragraphs: Predicting a property of an entire large graph requires information from across that graph, but training memory is limited. Graph Segment Training addresses this tension by dividing the graph into segments and backpropagating through only a few sampled segments in each iteration. The framework is designed to support training with a constant memory footprint.

A historical embedding table supplies representations for segments that are not currently selected for backpropagation. This makes their information available without recomputing all of their training paths, but stored embeddings can become stale. The method addresses this with two additions: finetuning the prediction head to correct input distribution shift, and Stale Embedding Dropout to reduce bias by dropping some outdated representations.

The complete method, GST-EFD, combines these components. Evaluations on MalNet and TpuGraphs find that it is memory-efficient and fast, with a slight test-accuracy improvement over a typical full-graph training regime. The findings show that selective gradient computation can retain useful whole-graph information when paired with explicit handling of stored representations.
neurips-2023-learning-large-graph-proper.tldr: Graph Segment Training reduces training memory by updating sampled graph segments and reusing stored embeddings with corrections for staleness.

paragraphs: Elastic full waveform inversion uses seismic information to characterize subsurface properties, including P-wave and S-wave velocities. These properties matter for applications such as carbon dioxide storage and energy exploration. This paper introduces EFWI, a benchmark collection designed specifically for learning and evaluating elastic inversion across varied geological structures.

The collection contains eight datasets, including structures with flat layers, curves, and faults, and supplies benchmark results from three deep learning methods. Compared with the authors' earlier acoustic OpenFWI dataset, its seismic observations include both horizontal and vertical components. Its target velocity maps also contain both P-wave and S-wave velocities, adding another physical quantity to recover.

These additions make the data more realistic while increasing difficulties with inversion convergence and computational cost. Numerical experiments investigate how P-wave and S-wave velocities relate in the seismic data, a relationship relevant to properties such as lithology, porosity, and fluid content. The benchmark is intended to support future multiparameter inversion research, including work connected to carbon-zero and new-energy applications.
neurips-2023-mathbf-mathbb-e-fwi-multipa.tldr: EFWI provides eight elastic seismic inversion datasets with multicomponent observations, P- and S-wave targets, and deep learning benchmarks.

paragraphs: Energy-based models offer a flexible way to describe complex data distributions, but training them and drawing samples remain difficult. Denoising score matching makes training scalable, yet the paper identifies an inconsistency: the learned energy model describes a noisy data distribution. That creates a gap between the trained distribution and the underlying clean distribution of interest.

The authors propose a sampling framework that combines moment matching with Gibbs or pseudo-Gibbs sampling. Its starting point is a noisy model that has already been trained well through denoising score matching. Given that starting point, the framework enables effective sampling from the underlying clean model, addressing the mismatch at the sampling stage.

The paper examines benefits relative to related methods and demonstrates how the approach can scale to high-dimensional datasets. Its significance is the connection between an accessible training procedure and the clean samples ultimately desired. The stated result depends on having a well-trained noisy model; the framework uses that model as the basis for recovering samples from the clean one.
neurips-2023-moment-matching-denoising-g.tldr: Moment-matching Gibbs-style sampling extracts clean-model samples from a noisy energy model well trained with denoising score matching.

paragraphs: In linear contextual bandits, observed rewards may contain different amounts of noise at different rounds. An algorithm should ideally benefit when rewards are more predictable, even when their noise variance is unknown. This paper proposes a Thompson Sampling-style method whose regret guarantee adapts to the accumulated reward variance.

Up to logarithmic factors, the bound is d^(3/2) times one plus the square root of the sum of the roundwise variances. Here d is the context-vector dimension. Expressing the guarantee through total variance connects the cost of learning to the noise actually present, rather than relying only on the number of rounds.

With constant-variance noise, the result recovers the existing d^(3/2) times square-root-of-T guarantee. For deterministic rewards, it improves to d^(3/2), up to logarithmic factors, and smoothly interpolates between those regimes. The method uses stratified sampling to address overly conservative optimism in linear Thompson Sampling. The contribution is a variance-sensitive theoretical guarantee covering both noisy and deterministic reward settings within one algorithmic approach.
neurips-2023-noise-adaptive-thompson-sam.tldr: A noise-adaptive Thompson Sampling method achieves regret bounds that improve as accumulated reward variance decreases.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning agents can struggle when environments contain changing or adversarial disturbances that their policies do not model. This paper also identifies an optimization difficulty: even linear policies based on state can lead to nonconvex objectives in linear dynamical systems. It develops an alternative family of policies organized around disturbance-related signals.

The authors define several kinds of signals called pseudo-disturbances and construct corresponding policy classes. Inspired by model-based control, these classes support efficient, practical optimization algorithms in a model-free setting. The resulting methods can integrate with any black-box model-free approach, providing a way to adapt an existing agent online when disturbances are adversarial.

For linear dynamics, the paper proves regret guarantees that improve the best-known bandit linear control results by removing dependence on state-space dimension. That theoretical claim is specifically tied to linear dynamics. Evaluations across standard reinforcement learning benchmarks also show improved robustness. Together, the analysis and experiments support disturbance-centered adaptation as a useful design principle for agents operating under changing conditions.
neurips-2023-online-nonstochastic-model-.tldr: Policies based on pseudo-disturbances improve online robustness and obtain state-dimension-independent regret guarantees for linear dynamics.

paragraphs: Images communicate relationships, but extracting those relationships into predefined tuples or a fixed vocabulary can limit what a system expresses. This paper explores open visual knowledge extraction, where the output is not confined to such formats. Its OpenVik system combines region detection with generation from a large multimodality model.

The first component finds image regions likely to contain relational knowledge. The second uses a detected region of interest to prompt the multimodality model, which generates format-free knowledge about it. This connects the generation process to image areas selected for their relational content. The authors also investigate two data enhancement techniques intended to diversify the generated knowledge.

Quality evaluations highlight the correctness and uniqueness of OpenVik's extracted knowledge. The authors additionally integrate that knowledge into multiple visual reasoning applications and report consistent improvements. These results support the usefulness of more expressive visual knowledge beyond its quality as standalone output. The work presents an initial exploration of this extraction paradigm and evidence that its outputs can benefit downstream reasoning.
neurips-2023-open-visual-knowledge-extra.tldr: OpenVik extracts format-free relational knowledge by prompting a multimodality model with selected image regions.

paragraphs: Adversarial training fits a model against worst-case perturbations of its training inputs. This paper studies linear regression, where the resulting optimization problem is convex, to understand how that training relates to familiar regularization methods. The analysis identifies several equivalences, each tied to particular conditions.

When there are more parameters than data points, adversarial training yields a minimum-norm interpolating solution if the maximum disturbance radius is below a threshold. Conversely, a minimum-norm interpolator solves an adversarial training problem with a corresponding radius. In the underparameterized regime, equivalence with ridge regression or Lasso can occur for suitable radii when covariates have a zero-mean symmetric distribution.

A further result concerns attacks bounded in the infinity norm. As with square-root Lasso, the disturbance radius used to obtain optimal bounds need not depend on additive noise variance. Numerical examples confirm the theoretical findings. The results explain how robustness to input perturbations can impose recognizable preferences on fitted parameters, while making clear that the particular preference depends on the regime, perturbation choice, and distributional conditions.
neurips-2023-regularization-properties-o.tldr: Under specified conditions, adversarial linear regression connects to minimum-norm interpolation, ridge regression, and Lasso.

paragraphs: Representing a scene as object slots is only part of predicting how it will change. A model must also account for interactions among objects. Reusable Slotwise Mechanisms addresses this by combining communication between slots with a modular system that dynamically selects mechanisms for predicting each slot's future state.

The reusable mechanisms receive information through Central Contextual Information, a bottleneck that gives a selected mechanism access to the remaining slots. This enables modeling of complex, higher-order interactions that may involve a sparse subset of objects. The architecture therefore connects predictions about individual objects with contextual information about the wider scene.

Experiments show stronger performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods on future prediction and related tasks, including visual question answering and action planning. The authors also demonstrate out-of-distribution generalization in intricate scenes. These findings support using dynamically selected, reusable interaction mechanisms alongside object-centered representations. The empirical contribution concerns both predicting object dynamics and using those predictions in tasks that require reasoning about what happens next.
neurips-2023-reusable-slotwise-mechanism.tldr: Reusable Slotwise Mechanisms predicts object dynamics through dynamically selected modules that share scene context through a bottleneck.

paragraphs: Sample-based explanations connect a model's prediction to particular training examples. This paper introduces generalized representers, a class of explanations that separates a training example's overall importance from its relevance to the specific test example. That separation provides a shared structure for reasoning about how training data contributes to individual predictions.

The global component assigns importance to a training point independently of which test point is being explained. The local component uses a kernel to measure similarity between the training and test points. The authors show that generalized representers are the only class satisfying their chosen set of natural axiomatic properties. This uniqueness is conditional on those properties.

The paper discusses how to extract global importance values for a given kernel and how to choose kernels for modern nonlinear models. It also shows that many popular explanation methods fit this framework through particular choices of these components. Empirical comparisons on two image classification datasets examine different generalized representers. The contribution supplies both an axiomatic characterization and a common language for comparing existing sample-based explanations.
neurips-2023-sample-based-explanations-v.tldr: Generalized representers unify sample-based explanations through global training-point importance and local kernel similarity.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks approximate solutions to partial differential equations, but difficult multidimensional problems can require many collocation points. Processing those points creates substantial computation and memory costs. This paper introduces separable PINNs, or SPINN, with an architecture and training procedure designed to reduce that burden.

SPINN processes coordinates on a per-axis basis, reducing the number of network propagations compared with conventional pointwise processing. It also uses forward-mode automatic differentiation to lower the cost of computing equation residuals. Together, these choices enable more than ten million collocation points on a single commodity GPU.

For the evaluated multidimensional equations, the paper reports 62-fold lower wall-clock cost and 1,394-fold fewer floating-point operations at the same number of collocation points, while improving accuracy. It also solves a chaotic two-space-plus-one-time Navier–Stokes problem in nine minutes versus ten hours for the best-performing prior method on a single GPU, while maintaining accuracy. A further demonstration accurately solves a three-space-plus-one-time Navier–Stokes problem, showing applicability to a demanding nonlinear setting.
neurips-2023-separable-physics-informed-.tldr: SPINN combines per-axis processing with forward-mode differentiation to substantially reduce the cost of solving multidimensional PDEs.

paragraphs: First-order optimization methods can target different measures of progress: reducing the function value or reducing the gradient magnitude. This paper introduces H-duality, a one-to-one correspondence between methods that efficiently pursue these two objectives. It offers a way to understand relationships among algorithms whose performance is usually assessed using different criteria.

In a continuous-time description, the correspondence arises by reversing the time dependence of the dissipation, or friction, term. This gives the algorithmic relationship a dynamical interpretation. The authors distinguish H-duality from Lagrange and Fenchel duality and, to their knowledge, from previously established duality or symmetry relations.

The framework clarifies the symmetry between Nesterov's method and OGM-G. It also leads to a new family of methods that efficiently reduce gradient magnitudes for smooth convex functions. For composite minimization, the authors derive a method described as simpler and faster than FISTA-G. Thus, the contribution both explains existing algorithms and supplies a route to new ones, with the stated results situated in convex optimization.
neurips-2023-time-reversed-dissipation-i.tldr: H-duality links efficient function-value and gradient-magnitude minimization methods through time reversal of dissipation.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning can tolerate biased negative samples, including examples with similar semantics. This paper explains that behavior through distributionally robust optimization. In this view, contrastive learning optimizes against a range of possible negative-sampling distributions, helping account for robustness when the sampled negatives do not match an ideal distribution.

The analysis gives temperature a precise role: it acts as a Lagrange coefficient controlling the size of that distribution set. The authors also connect distributionally robust optimization with mutual information. This supplies further theoretical support for interpreting InfoNCE as a mutual-information estimate and provides an estimation approach for generalized mutual information based on phi-divergences.

The same perspective exposes possible weaknesses, including excessive conservatism and sensitivity to outliers. The proposed Adjusted InfoNCE loss, ADNCE, refines the potential distribution to mitigate these issues. Experiments involving images, sentences, and graphs validate the approach, with reported performance improvements and faster convergence. The contribution combines an explanation of existing robustness with a loss modification motivated by the drawbacks revealed through that explanation.
neurips-2023-understanding-contrastive-l.tldr: A distributionally robust view explains contrastive learning's sampling-bias tolerance and motivates an adjusted InfoNCE loss.
